title: List scheduling the c = a + b dependence DAG
summary_caption: List scheduling: each cycle, issue the highest-priority ready node. Overlapping the two independent loads hid a cycle of load latency.

frames.caption: The dependence DAG for c = a + b (note section 1): the add needs both loads, the store needs the add. Assume loads take 2 cycles, add and store 1.
Ready set = nodes with no unscheduled predecessors: ld a and ld b. The add and store must wait for their operands.
Cycle 0 — pick by priority (critical-path length; the loads tie): issue ld a. Its 2-cycle latency means the result arrives at cycle 2.
Cycle 1 — ld a is still in flight, but ld b is independent and ready: issue it now instead of idling. This is latency hiding.
Cycle 2 — add is the only candidate, but ld b's result only lands at cycle 3. Nothing is ready: the scheduler stalls one cycle.
Cycle 3 — both operands have arrived: issue the add. The store becomes the next ready node.
Cycle 4 — the add's result is ready: issue st c. The DAG is fully scheduled in 5 cycles.
Payoff: had ld b waited for ld a to finish, it would issue at cycle 2 and the store at cycle 5 — 6 cycles. Overlapping the loads saved one.
